overview: Bonanza Peak is the highest non-volcanic summit in Washington and the Chelan County highpoint, deep in the Glacier Peak Wilderness above Holden Village. This line is the peak's standard east-side route: roped travel up the Mary Green Glacier, then loose Class 3-4 scrambling through a gully/rib system to a notch on the upper northeast ridge and a short, exposed crest to the summit.
beta: From Holden Village, hike the Railroad Creek and Holden Lake trails to camp at Holden Lake or Holden Pass. Cross the Mary Green Glacier to the rock, weave between the two gully/rib lines to the notch on the upper ridge, and follow the crest to the summit. Descend the same route.

Summit ridge: Class 3-4

overview: Bulls Tooth is a striking granite summit on the arcuate ridge rimming Chain and Doelle Lakes in the Chiwaukum Mountains, about 5.5 miles southeast of Stevens Pass in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness (Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest). It's one of the longest approaches out of Stevens Pass -- roughly 10 miles one-way via the PCT, Icicle Creek Trail, and the steep, unswitchbacked Chain Lakes Trail (#1569) -- rewarding backpackers with a quiet basin and a short, airy Class 3 scramble to a broad summit
beta: Bulls Tooth has no maintained summit trail. Parties reach the base via the Chain Lakes basin — a scenic, blueberry-covered alpine bench in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness — then climb through steep heather, mossy slabs, brush, and short cliff bands to boulder fields below the summit block, finishing on a short, exposed Class 3 pitch of looser, sandier rock near the top. Route-finding is the main challenge; there is no cairned or established line.
breakdown: Chain Lakes to boulder fields: Class 2-3
Boulder fields to summit: Class 3
flagged: Another party calls the Class 4-5 south ridge 'undoubtedly the easiest way' up the Tooth, so it is unclear that a separate Class 3 north-notch route exists as described.

overview: Chimney Rock is a steep peak on the Cascade Crest in the Alpine Lakes Wilderness with three summits: the central spire (7,727 ft) is the highest, the north peak is 7,634 ft, and the minor south peak is 7,440 ft. This line climbs the south peak. From the Chimney Glacier it takes wet fourth-class ground and ledges up the east side to the notch between the central and south summits, then continues about 400 ft to the top.
beta: From the upper Chimney Glacier, cross the moat at the foot of the rock and climb the face to the left of the main gully that drops from the notch between the central and south summits. About three pitches of wet, slippery fourth-class ground lead to a system of ledges, some of them very wide, that runs up to just below the notch, roughly 600 vertical ft above the glacier. From the notch, climb about 400 ft more to the South Peak. Stoppers and slings are enough protection.

overview: Hidden Couloir is the entry gully of Dragontail's north-face ice and mixed complex — it is the first of the three couloirs linked by the popular Triple Couloirs route. It starts around 6,400 ft directly above the south end of Colchuck Lake and, true to its name, is hidden from view from the lake itself.
